claim: For the Bakim (2026) two-community mean-field opinion model with equal community fractions, cubic amplification, and interaction cutoff \(0<\varepsilon\leq1\), every locally asymptotically stable strictly interacting ordered-polar equilibrium is the unique symmetric branch of gap \(\delta=\sqrt{1-2\beta/\alpha}\). Such a stable equilibrium exists if and only if \(\varepsilon>1/\sqrt3\), \(\alpha>3\beta\), and \(1-2\beta/\alpha<\varepsilon^2\). For \(2\beta<\alpha<3\beta\), the symmetric polar branch is a full-system saddle whenever it lies inside the confidence region; at \(\alpha=3\beta\) it is nonlinearly unstable whenever it is an interacting equilibrium. If \(\alpha>3\beta\), the remaining two ordered interacting polarized equilibria, when admitted by confidence, are asymmetric saddles with shifted midpoint square \(s^2=(1-3\beta/\alpha)/4\) and gap square \(d^2=(1+\beta/\alpha)/4\). No other strictly interacting ordered-polar equilibria exist. This gives a sharp confidence-feasibility barrier and corrects the full-dimensional stability interpretation of the source invariant-gap bifurcation.
integrity: Symbolic identities and boundary arguments are independently reconstructed from the explicit printed equations; accompanying verifier is supporting evidence, not a proof of universal statements.
scientific_limitations: Only deterministic equal-group-size two-community mean-field cubic equations and ordinary equilibria strictly inside the interacting region.
No claim of global convergence, basin prevalence, heterogeneous group stability, agent-based dynamics, or Filippov sliding.
The source polar-gap formula on the invariant midpoint line is retained; only the full two-dimensional stability is reclassified.
Unindexed broader exchange-symmetric coupled-cubic normal-form classifications may contain related statements.
title: A sharp transverse-stability barrier and ordered-polar equilibrium census for cubic opinion amplification
